{"type": "trajectory", "content": "[{\"role\": \"tool\", \"tool_call_id\": \"call_9zcGGJjMMw5TN7axadrQoWnS\", \"content\": \"{\\\"type\\\": \\\"text\\\", \\\"file\\\": {\\\"filePath\\\": \\\"/home/novix/workspace/writing_space/drafts/v1_draft.tex\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"\\\\\\\\documentclass[11pt,a4paper]{article}\\\\n\\\\\\\\usepackage[margin=24mm]{geometry}\\\\n\\\\\\\\usepackage{fontspec}\\\\n\\\\\\\\setmainfont{DejaVu Serif}\\\\\\\\setsansfont{DejaVu Sans}\\\\n\\\\\\\\usepackage{graphicx,booktabs,tabularx,array,amsmath,enumitem}\\\\n\\\\\\\\usepackage[numbers,sort&compress]{natbib}\\\\n\\\\\\\\usepackage[colorlinks=true,linkcolor=black,citecolor=black,urlcolor=black]{hyperref}\\\\n\\\\\\\\usepackage{fancyhdr}\\\\n\\\\\\\\graphicspath{{../figures/}}\\\\n\\\\\\\\setlength{\\\\\\\\parindent}{0pt}\\\\\\\\setlength{\\\\\\\\parskip}{5pt}\\\\n\\\\\\\\setlength{\\\\\\\\emergencystretch}{3em}\\\\n\\\\\\\\pagestyle{fancy}\\\\\\\\fancyhf{}\\\\\\\\fancyhead[L]{\\\\\\\\small Attention sinks in small language models}\\\\\\\\fancyhead[R]{\\\\\\\\small Research idea brief}\\\\\\\\fancyfoot[C]{\\\\\\\\thepage}\\\\n\\\\\\\\newcolumntype{Y}{>{\\\\\\\\raggedright\\\\\\\\arraybackslash}X}\\\\n\\\\\\\\title{Attention Sinks in Small Language Models\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\large A Research-Backed Idea Tree and Three Testable Projects}\\\\n\\\\\\\\author{Research ideation brief}\\\\\\\\date{Evidence cutoff: 11 October 2026}\\\\n\\\\\\\\begin{document}\\\\n\\\\\\\\maketitle\\\\n\\\\\\\\begin{abstract}\\\\nAttention sinks are already documented in very small language models, making simple existence tests a weak novelty claim. This brief accompanies a persistent idea tree built through five research-and-gating rounds. Three families survived: causal function diagnostics, precision robustness, and streaming boundary behavior. The strongest finalist asks whether separate routing and value-path interventions predict held-out harm from sink removal better than attention mass alone. A second isolates transient anchor-switch shocks using position-correct factorial controls. A third tests the noninferiority of lowering sink-value precision near cache evictions, with actual byte accounting and an early termination rule for negligible savings. These are proposals, not experimental findings. The contribution of each is deliberately narrower than existing circuit analyses, sink/content metrics, asymmetric KV quantization, SubKV, KVSink, and streaming stability protocols. Novelty remains provisional; recent preprints are treated as scoped evidence, and a withdrawn quantization paper is excluded from support.\\\\n\\\\\\\\end{abstract}\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\section{Framing and research process}\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{What the question should become}\\\\nAn attention sink is a position that attracts disproportionate attention across later queries, often an initial token. High attention does not by itself show that the token supplies useful semantic content. Gu et al. establish the phenomenon in small models, including their tiny Pythia examples, and study its emergence under optimization, data, objectives, and architecture \\\\\\\\citep{gu2025}. StreamingLLM already includes a 160M-parameter experiment with a dedicated sink token \\\\\\\\citep{xiao2024}. Consequently, neither ``small models have sinks'' nor ``add a sink token to a small model'' is a defensible headline contribution here.\\\\n\\\\nWe use approximately 0.1--3B parameters as a working scope, not a universal definition of a small language model. The first pilots should use public 124M--1B models, followed by a current 1--3B rotary model only after a configuration audit. The important axes are architecture, training exposure, tokenizer behavior, positional encoding, KV-head sharing, and deployment backend. Parameter count alone cannot identify a mechanism. Pythia is useful because its public training checkpoints and controlled data ordering enable within-family trajectory analyses \\\\\\\\citep{pythia2023}; it does not eliminate all depth/width confounding across sizes.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Search, filtering, and persistence}\\\\nResearch was performed through MCP paper searches, scholarly aggregation, Google discovery, paper-fulltext retrieval, and repository or publisher-page verification. Search angles covered sink emergence, small-model causal diagnostics, value versus key functions, quantization, session resets, and retrieval. Discovery is targeted and iterative, not a PRISMA-style systematic review. Broad searches returned unrelated Crossref and arXiv hits; those were excluded. The saved search cache is a discovery ledger, not an automatically trusted bibliography.\\\\n\\\\nFive expansion rounds produced three root children, two approaches per family, and three deeper finalist protocols: 13 nodes including the root, with finalists at depth three edges from the root. Each mutation was executed by treejson 0.3.0-novix.2; the tree was never directly written or edited. Each round ended with structural validation reporting valid=true and no warnings. Node fields are limited to summary, description, next\\\\\\\\_action, and references. Novelty, gap, feasibility, and reference judgments are recorded in separate round specifications and embedded prose rather than extra tree fields.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\section{Established evidence and novelty boundaries}\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Mechanisms: distinguish observation, construction, and function}\\\\nThe evidence supports a heterogeneous question rather than a single universal explanation. Gu et al. describe sink keys as bias-like destinations for surplus attention and connect the effect partly to softmax normalization \\\\\\\\citep{gu2025}. Barbero et al. argue that sinks help counter over-mixing, relating them to information propagation through depth and context \\\\\\\\citep{barbero2025}. These explanations concern different levels: how a sink is constructed and why its behavior may be useful need not be identical.\\\\n\\\\nA 2026 GPT-2 study identifies an interacting query-bias, positional-MLP, and key-projection circuit in the 124M model. Its authors explicitly emphasize that components are dispensable in other architectures that still exhibit sinks \\\\\\\\citep{ranmilo2026}. Recent work links sink behavior to self-concentration and value-non-mixing, while another studies absolute-position signals in rotary models \\\\\\\\citep{kiya2026,ruscio2026}. These studies motivate architecture-stratified interventions; they do not license using a GPT-2 bias ablation as a universal sink-removal recipe.\\\\n\\\\nFesser et al. distinguish adaptive no-operation and broadcast computations and perform causal tests, primarily in vision transformers \\\\\\\\citep{fesser2026}. In a causal decoder, the first token cannot aggregate future tokens. A nonzero first-token value can transmit a static token-dependent component, but calling it a future-content broadcast hub would violate the mask. The finalist therefore measures routing and output-projected value contribution without forcing all heads into two labels. Attention-causal communication methods are also prior art, not a newly invented causal discovery concept \\\\\\\\citep{franco2025}.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Metrics, compression, and streaming: crowded areas}\\\\nSink mass and content allocation must be reported separately. Recent compositional-data work shows that retaining versus removing the sink coordinate changes what standard metrics estimate, and already studies prediction and pruning consequences \\\\\\\\citep{papamichalis2026}. We reuse its sink/content distinction rather than present entropy separation as novel. Recent SinkProbe work is treated as related diagnostic work, not evidence that a small-model pilot validates million-token production behavior \\\\\\\\citep{rizwan2026}. Gradient-sink work reports a training-time intervention preserving sinks while reducing massive activations in its tested RMSNorm setting \\\\\\\\citep{chen2026}; that prevents treating raw activation magnitude as a universal proxy for sink dependence.\\\\n\\\\nQuantization is particularly crowded. CushionCache prefixes mitigate activation outliers, KIVI uses different quantization axes for keys and values, SKVQ preserves recent high-precision states, and key-favored bit allocation is already studied \\\\\\\\citep{son2024,kivi2024,skvq2024,hariri2025}. KVSink detects sinks beyond the first positions, and SubKV explicitly targets sub-billion models with sink-aware quantization \\\\\\\\citep{kvsink2025,subkv2025}. A project cannot claim either ``small-model sink protection'' or ``give keys more bits'' as its new idea.\\\\n\\\\nStreamingLLM distinguishes continuous stable generation from extending memory of historical content \\\\\\\\citep{xiao2024}. ThreeH later formalizes stability, access, and utility horizons \\\\\\\\citep{cao2026}. SinkRouter already uses low-impact sink-associated updates to selectively bypass head computation, with dedicated kernels and larger tested models \\\\\\\\citep{sinkrouter2026}. Our proposals instead examine small-model counterfactual harm and boundary-local transients. They do not introduce the stability/recall distinction or generic sink-aware routing.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\begin{table}[ht]\\\\n\\\\\\\\centering\\\\\\\\small\\\\n\\\\\\\\begin{tabularx}{\\\\\\\\linewidth}{@{}p{3.2cm}YY@{}}\\\\n\\\\\\\\toprule\\\\nEstablished direction & Why an obvious idea is rejected & Surviving narrower target\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\midrule\\\\nSink emergence in small LMs \\\\\\\\citep{gu2025} & Existence and generic size sweeps are already studied. & Prospective intervention-harm prediction.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNOP and circuit diagnostics \\\\\\\\citep{ranmilo2026,fesser2026} & Mechanistic labels and interventions are prior art. & Separate-document prediction and cross-family failure attribution.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nSink-aware low-bit caches \\\\\\\\citep{kvsink2025,subkv2025} & Both noninitial sinks and sub-billion deployment are covered. & Boundary-stratified, held-out safe/unsafe V-downgrade map.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nStable streaming \\\\\\\\citep{xiao2024,cao2026} & Stability is not new memory capacity. & Anchor-switch transient attribution at identical suffix state.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\bottomrule\\\\n\\\\\\\\end{tabularx}\\\\n\\\\\\\\caption{Novelty boundaries used to reject or narrow candidates. These are research judgments, not exhaustive priority claims.}\\\\n\\\\\\\\end{table}\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\section{Approach landscape and candidate gates}\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Three families and six surviving approaches}\\\\nThe causal family contains a removal-harm predictor and a checkpoint trajectory study separating cache dependence from sink mass and outliers. The compression family contains a sink-value precision certificate and a domain/prefix calibration-shift stress test. The streaming family contains an anchor-switch shock audit and an oracle-retrieval interaction study. All six pass a provisional gap and feasibility screen, but only the first approach in each family is developed into an implementation-ready leaf.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\begin{figure}[ht]\\\\n\\\\\\\\centering\\\\\\\\includegraphics[width=\\\\\\\\linewidth]{attention-sinks-fig01-research-map.png}\\\\n\\\\\\\\caption{Explanatory research map: three families refine into three deeper finalists. Arrows represent ideation refinement, not measured causal relationships. No model experiments were run for this brief.}\\\\n\\\\\\\\label{fig:map}\\\\n\\\\\\\\end{figure}\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Why these branches passed and others did not}\\\\nThe retained branches have a concrete differential question, named overlapping work, an inference-first path, and a failure criterion. References motivate the question but do not prove the proposed effect. Negative outcomes remain informative: inability to predict harm, absence of an anchor-specific shock, or an economically negligible precision saving are valid deliverables. This makes the projects less vulnerable to post-hoc storytelling.\\\\n\\\\nRejected candidates included a generic first-token heatmap survey; a new dedicated sink prefix; a blanket keep-first-four quantization rule; unrestricted gating pretraining; sink-based hallucination detection without confound controls; and treating anchors as unlimited memory. The first three overlap directly with established work, the fourth has disproportionate training and kernel cost for this scoped task, and the final two risk unsupported causal or capacity claims. The search also located HeadQ (arXiv:2605.03562), whose current repository record states that it is withdrawn for ethical concerns. Its abstract was useful only as an overlap warning; its results are not used as evidence and it is excluded from the bibliography.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\section{Three implementation-ready finalist protocols}\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Priority 1: predict harm from removing sinks}\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Question and hypothesis.} Can routing/value response signatures measured on development documents predict held-out joint anchor-deletion harm better than sink attention mass alone? The incremental novelty is prospective, separate-document harm prediction across selected small-model families. Existing circuit analysis, NOP tests, compositional metrics, and attention-causal methods remain explicit baselines \\\\\\\\citep{ranmilo2026,fesser2026,papamichalis2026,franco2025}.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Pilot.} Pin revisions of GPT-2 124M and Pythia 160M, 410M, and 1B. Use 100 development and 200 disjoint test documents at lengths 128 and 512, with three sampling seeds. Seeds vary fixture selection; they do not turn one pretrained checkpoint into three independently trained models. Keep tokenization and model-supported position conventions fixed within every paired comparison.\\\\n\\\\nAt a selected layer/head, zero only the sink value while preserving its key, perturb only the sink key using a same-layer norm-matched nonsink key, and run a sham patch. Check that the local attention weights are unchanged by the value-only intervention; later layers may change because their inputs have changed. Features include output-projected sink contribution, key-perturbation sensitivity, sink mass, and conditional content entropy. The target is excess next-token negative log likelihood (NLL) after a distinct intervention---joint removal of retained anchor states---on independent test documents. Training and scoring on the same intervention and documents would make the predictor tautological and is prohibited.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Controls and acceptance.} Fit a regularized predictor on development data only. Compare its test mean absolute error (MAE) with mass-only, norm-only, and feature-ablated baselines. Use document-cluster bootstrap for paired error differences. Freeze thresholds and head selection before test evaluation, include matched random-token and sham patches, and restore original K/V for rescue checks. Go forward only when the paired interval for MAE improvement excludes zero and controls are consistent with the claimed attribution. Leave-family-out transfer is exploratory because the family count is small. If it fails, release the error analysis rather than claim a universal sink classifier.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Priority 2: attribute anchor-switch boundary shocks}\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Question and hypothesis.} Does changing retained anchors create a short-lived predictive loss increase beyond suffix-recomputation effects? This is not another demonstration that keeping sinks stabilizes streaming. It isolates a counterfactual at a boundary, acknowledging that cache-local rotary positions and the origin of the first state matter \\\\\\\\citep{xiao2024,ruscio2026,kiya2026}.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Pilot.} Start with Pythia 160M, 410M, and 1B, a 512-position cache containing four anchors and a 508-token recent suffix, and prose/code streams up to 16K tokens. This is bounded-cache streaming, not a 16K dense-context claim. At declared boundaries, cross original versus fresh-session anchor states with reused versus fresh-session-recomputed suffix states. The mixed-state arms are diagnostic interventions, not production reset policies. Every arm uses the same model revision and isolated session; no cross-user state is shared.\\\\n\\\\nWithin each suffix-state arm, hold suffix tensors and cache-local positions identical. Generate keys before RoPE or correctly undo and reapply rotations when assigning positions. Test the unchanged-state path against a no-op implementation for numerical agreement. Absolute-position GPT-2 is not used for this streaming remapping experiment. Fresh recomputation must use the same intended retained input and no hidden information unavailable to the comparison arm.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Controls and acceptance.} The primary endpoint is positive excess-NLL area over the first 64 post-boundary tokens relative to that suffix arm's unchanged-anchor control. Also report peak excess loss and recovery: the first point after which loss remains within a development-fixed tolerance for a prespecified run of tokens. Analyze the signed difference too, so positive-part integration cannot conceal improvements. Sample 200 held-out stream boundaries, bootstrap by document rather than boundary, and report prose/code strata. Go forward only when an effect exceeds a development-fixed practical threshold, its interval excludes zero, and position/backend and matched nonsink-patch controls do not explain it. Otherwise reject anchor-specific attribution or identify an implementation defect. No old-fact recall gain is inferred from lower NLL \\\\\\\\citep{cao2026}.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Priority 3: certify or refute sink-value precision downgrades}\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Question and hypothesis.} Can selected sink KV groups use lower-precision values while preserving keys, without practically important excess loss near eviction? The contribution is a held-out, boundary-stratified safe/unsafe map, not asymmetric precision, a new sink detector, or small-model quantization itself \\\\\\\\citep{kivi2024,hariri2025,kvsink2025,subkv2025}.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Pilot.} Use Pythia 410M and 1B first, with cache capacities 256 and 512. Optionally add a current rotary grouped-query model after its configuration and kernels are audited. Evaluate K16/V16, K16/V4, K4/V16, and K4/V4 for protected groups while holding nonsink quantizers fixed. Use established per-channel key and per-token value axes, record pre-/post-RoPE choices, clipping, group size, scale storage, and zero points. In grouped-query attention (GQA), KV states are shared by query heads: policies must select KV groups, not pretend that each query head has independently stored keys and values.\\\\n\\\\nFreeze a group selection policy on development documents, then evaluate 200 independent held-out streams, domain shifts, and the 64-token post-eviction window. Compare first-N protection, KVSink, SubKV, random protection, recent-token protection, and symmetric sink preservation. Numerical sensitivity tests may first hold the set of cached tokens constant; deployment comparisons must additionally match total actual bytes by adjusting the cache budget or precision allocation. These are different experiments and should not be mixed in one superiority claim.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Acceptance and early exit.} A candidate downgrade passes numerical noninferiority only if the upper one-sided 95\\\\\\\\% document-bootstrap bound for excess NLL relative to symmetric protection is below a preregistered 0.01 nats/token margin. That margin is a proposed engineering tolerance, not a literature-established standard. Prespecified domain/boundary strata must also satisfy it; use a simultaneous bootstrap upper bound across strata, or a conservative multiplicity adjustment. An engineering go additionally requires at least 1\\\\\\\\% measured total-cache savings and no latency regression in a real backend. Fake quantization demonstrates sensitivity, not storage reduction or throughput.\\\\n\\\\nBefore implementation, bound possible savings. For a 512-token cache, four protected tokens, otherwise K4/V4, and protected K16/V16, payload bits per shared layer/head dimension are $508(4+4)+4(16+16)=4192$. Lowering only four protected values from 16 to 4 bits saves $4(16-4)=48$ bits per dimension, or about 1.15\\\\\\\\% of this payload. At 4096 tokens the same change is roughly 0.15\\\\\\\\%. Removing a token's direct KV entry removes direct access to that entry, but later cached states were computed from its past context and may contain indirect traces. Fluent indefinite streaming is never equated with indefinite factual recall \\\\\\\\citep{xiao2024,cao2026}.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Resource envelope and staging}\\\\nThe preferred work is inference-only. {"type": "trajectory", "content": "[{\"role\": \"tool\", \"tool_call_id\": \"call_9NjBE6zhJIiA8pyM6xTrvM7Y\", \"content\": \"{\\\"type\\\": \\\"text\\\", \\\"file\\\": {\\\"filePath\\\": \\\"/home/novix/workspace/writing_space/drafts/v2_draft.tex\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"\\\\\\\\documentclass[11pt,a4paper]{article}\\\\n\\\\\\\\usepackage[margin=24mm]{geometry}\\\\n\\\\\\\\usepackage{fontspec}\\\\n\\\\\\\\setmainfont{DejaVu Serif}\\\\\\\\setsansfont{DejaVu Sans}\\\\n\\\\\\\\usepackage{graphicx,booktabs,tabularx,array,amsmath,enumitem}\\\\n\\\\\\\\usepackage[numbers,sort&compress]{natbib}\\\\n\\\\\\\\usepackage[colorlinks=true,linkcolor=black,citecolor=black,urlcolor=black]{hyperref}\\\\n\\\\\\\\usepackage{fancyhdr}\\\\n\\\\\\\\graphicspath{{../figures/}}\\\\n\\\\\\\\setlength{\\\\\\\\parindent}{0pt}\\\\\\\\setlength{\\\\\\\\parskip}{5pt}\\\\n\\\\\\\\setlength{\\\\\\\\emergencystretch}{3em}\\\\n\\\\\\\\pagestyle{fancy}\\\\\\\\fancyhf{}\\\\\\\\fancyhead[L]{\\\\\\\\small Attention sinks in small language models}\\\\\\\\fancyhead[R]{\\\\\\\\small Research idea brief}\\\\\\\\fancyfoot[C]{\\\\\\\\thepage}\\\\n\\\\\\\\newcolumntype{Y}{>{\\\\\\\\raggedright\\\\\\\\arraybackslash}X}\\\\n\\\\\\\\title{Attention Sinks in Small Language Models\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\large A Research-Backed Idea Tree and Three Testable Projects}\\\\n\\\\\\\\author{Research ideation brief}\\\\\\\\date{Evidence cutoff: 11 October 2026}\\\\n\\\\\\\\begin{document}\\\\n\\\\\\\\maketitle\\\\n\\\\\\\\begin{abstract}\\\\nAttention sinks are already documented in very small language models, making simple existence tests a weak novelty claim. This brief accompanies a persistent idea tree built through five research-and-gating rounds. Three families survived: causal function diagnostics, precision robustness, and streaming boundary behavior. The strongest finalist asks whether separate routing and value-path interventions predict held-out harm from sink removal better than attention mass alone. A second isolates transient anchor-switch shocks using position-correct factorial controls. A third tests the noninferiority of lowering sink-value precision near cache evictions, with actual byte accounting and an early termination rule for negligible savings. These are proposals, not experimental findings. The contribution of each is deliberately narrower than existing circuit analyses, sink/content metrics, asymmetric KV quantization, SubKV, KVSink, and streaming stability protocols. Novelty remains provisional; recent preprints are treated as scoped evidence, and a withdrawn quantization paper is excluded from support.\\\\n\\\\\\\\end{abstract}\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\section{Framing and research process}\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{What the question should become}\\\\nAn attention sink is a position that attracts disproportionate attention across later queries, often an initial token. High attention does not by itself show that the token supplies useful semantic content. Gu et al. establish the phenomenon in small models, including their tiny Pythia examples, and study its emergence under optimization, data, objectives, and architecture \\\\\\\\citep{gu2025}. StreamingLLM already includes a 160M-parameter experiment with a dedicated sink token \\\\\\\\citep{xiao2024}. Consequently, neither ``small models have sinks'' nor ``add a sink token to a small model'' is a defensible headline contribution here.\\\\n\\\\nWe use approximately 0.1--3B parameters as a working scope, not a universal definition of a small language model. The first pilots should use public 124M--1B models, followed by a current 1--3B rotary model only after a configuration audit. The important axes are architecture, training exposure, tokenizer behavior, positional encoding, KV-head sharing, and deployment backend. Parameter count alone cannot identify a mechanism. Pythia is useful because its public training checkpoints and controlled data ordering enable within-family trajectory analyses \\\\\\\\citep{pythia2023}; it does not eliminate all depth/width confounding across sizes.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Search, filtering, and persistence}\\\\nResearch was performed through MCP paper searches, scholarly aggregation, Google discovery, paper-fulltext retrieval, and repository or publisher-page verification. Search angles covered sink emergence, small-model causal diagnostics, value versus key functions, quantization, session resets, and retrieval. Discovery is targeted and iterative, not a PRISMA-style systematic review. Broad searches returned unrelated Crossref and arXiv hits; those were excluded. The saved search cache is a discovery ledger, not an automatically trusted bibliography.\\\\n\\\\nFive expansion rounds produced three root children, two approaches per family, and three deeper finalist protocols: 13 nodes including the root, with finalists at depth three edges from the root. Each mutation was executed by treejson 0.3.0-novix.2; the tree was never directly written or edited. Each round ended with structural validation reporting valid=true and no warnings. Node fields are limited to summary, description, next\\\\\\\\_action, and references. Novelty, gap, feasibility, and reference judgments are recorded in separate round specifications and embedded prose rather than extra tree fields.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\section{Established evidence and novelty boundaries}\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Mechanisms: distinguish observation, construction, and function}\\\\nThe evidence supports a heterogeneous question rather than a single universal explanation. Gu et al. describe sink keys as bias-like destinations for surplus attention and connect the effect partly to softmax normalization \\\\\\\\citep{gu2025}. Barbero et al. argue that sinks help counter over-mixing, relating them to information propagation through depth and context \\\\\\\\citep{barbero2025}. These explanations concern different levels: how a sink is constructed and why its behavior may be useful need not be identical.\\\\n\\\\nA 2026 GPT-2 study identifies an interacting query-bias, positional-MLP, and key-projection circuit in the 124M model. Its authors explicitly emphasize that components are dispensable in other architectures that still exhibit sinks \\\\\\\\citep{ranmilo2026}. Recent work links sink behavior to self-concentration and value-non-mixing, while another studies absolute-position signals in rotary models \\\\\\\\citep{kiya2026,ruscio2026}. These studies motivate architecture-stratified interventions; they do not license using a GPT-2 bias ablation as a universal sink-removal recipe.\\\\n\\\\nFesser et al. distinguish adaptive no-operation and broadcast computations and perform causal tests, primarily in vision transformers \\\\\\\\citep{fesser2026}. In a causal decoder, the first token cannot aggregate future tokens. A nonzero first-token value can transmit a static token-dependent component, but calling it a future-content broadcast hub would violate the mask. The finalist therefore measures routing and output-projected value contribution without forcing all heads into two labels. Attention-causal communication methods are also prior art, not a newly invented causal discovery concept \\\\\\\\citep{franco2025}.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Metrics, compression, and streaming: crowded areas}\\\\nSink mass and content allocation must be reported separately. Recent compositional-data work shows that retaining versus removing the sink coordinate changes what standard metrics estimate, and already studies prediction and pruning consequences \\\\\\\\citep{papamichalis2026}. We reuse its sink/content distinction rather than present entropy separation as novel. Recent SinkProbe work is treated as related diagnostic work, not evidence that a small-model pilot validates million-token production behavior \\\\\\\\citep{rizwan2026}. Gradient-sink work reports a training-time intervention preserving sinks while reducing massive activations in its tested RMSNorm setting \\\\\\\\citep{chen2026}; that prevents treating raw activation magnitude as a universal proxy for sink dependence.\\\\n\\\\nQuantization is particularly crowded. CushionCache prefixes mitigate activation outliers, KIVI uses different quantization axes for keys and values, SKVQ preserves recent high-precision states, and key-favored bit allocation is already studied \\\\\\\\citep{son2024,kivi2024,skvq2024,hariri2025}. KVSink detects sinks beyond the first positions, and SubKV explicitly targets sub-billion models with sink-aware quantization \\\\\\\\citep{kvsink2025,subkv2025}. A project cannot claim either ``small-model sink protection'' or ``give keys more bits'' as its new idea.\\\\n\\\\nStreamingLLM distinguishes continuous stable generation from extending memory of historical content \\\\\\\\citep{xiao2024}. ThreeH later formalizes stability, access, and utility horizons \\\\\\\\citep{cao2026}. SinkRouter already uses low-impact sink-associated updates to selectively bypass head computation, with dedicated kernels and larger tested models \\\\\\\\citep{sinkrouter2026}. Our proposals instead examine small-model counterfactual harm and boundary-local transients. They do not introduce the stability/recall distinction or generic sink-aware routing.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\begin{table}[ht]\\\\n\\\\\\\\centering\\\\\\\\small\\\\n\\\\\\\\begin{tabularx}{\\\\\\\\linewidth}{@{}p{3.2cm}YY@{}}\\\\n\\\\\\\\toprule\\\\nEstablished direction & Why an obvious idea is rejected & Surviving narrower target\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\midrule\\\\nSink emergence in small LMs \\\\\\\\citep{gu2025} & Existence and generic size sweeps are already studied. & Prospective intervention-harm prediction.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNOP and circuit diagnostics \\\\\\\\citep{ranmilo2026,fesser2026} & Mechanistic labels and interventions are prior art. & Separate-document prediction and cross-family failure attribution.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nSink-aware low-bit caches \\\\\\\\citep{kvsink2025,subkv2025} & Both noninitial sinks and sub-billion deployment are covered. & Boundary-stratified, held-out V-downgrade noninferiority map.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nStable streaming \\\\\\\\citep{xiao2024,cao2026} & Stability is not new memory capacity. & Anchor-switch transient attribution at identical suffix state.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\bottomrule\\\\n\\\\\\\\end{tabularx}\\\\n\\\\\\\\caption{Novelty boundaries used to reject or narrow candidates. These are research judgments, not exhaustive priority claims.}\\\\n\\\\\\\\end{table}\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\section{Approach landscape and candidate gates}\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Three families and six surviving approaches}\\\\nThe causal family contains a removal-harm predictor and a checkpoint trajectory study separating cache dependence from sink mass and outliers. The compression family contains a sink-value precision noninferiority test and a domain/prefix calibration-shift stress test. The streaming family contains an anchor-switch shock audit and an oracle-retrieval interaction study. All six pass a provisional gap and feasibility screen, but only the first approach in each family is developed into an preregistration-ready leaf.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\begin{figure}[ht]\\\\n\\\\\\\\centering\\\\\\\\includegraphics[width=\\\\\\\\linewidth]{attention-sinks-fig01-research-map.png}\\\\n\\\\\\\\caption{Explanatory research map: three families refine into three deeper finalists. Arrows represent ideation refinement, not measured causal relationships. No model experiments were run for this brief.}\\\\n\\\\\\\\label{fig:map}\\\\n\\\\\\\\end{figure}\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Why these branches passed and others did not}\\\\nThe retained branches have a concrete differential question, named overlapping work, an inference-first path, and a failure criterion. References motivate the question but do not prove the proposed effect. Negative outcomes remain informative: inability to predict harm, absence of an anchor-specific shock, or an economically negligible precision saving are valid deliverables. This makes the projects less vulnerable to post-hoc storytelling.\\\\n\\\\nRejected candidates included a generic first-token heatmap survey; a new dedicated sink prefix; a blanket keep-first-four quantization rule; unrestricted gating pretraining; sink-based hallucination detection without confound controls; and treating anchors as unlimited memory. The first three overlap directly with established work, the fourth has disproportionate training and kernel cost for this scoped task, and the final two risk unsupported causal or capacity claims. The search also located HeadQ (arXiv:2605.03562), whose current repository record states that it is withdrawn for ethical concerns. Its abstract was useful only as an overlap warning; its results are not used as evidence and it is excluded from the bibliography.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\section{Three preregistration-ready finalist protocols}\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Priority 1: predict harm from removing sinks}\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Question and hypothesis.} Can routing/value response signatures measured on development documents predict held-out joint anchor-deletion harm better than sink attention mass alone? The incremental novelty is prospective, separate-document harm prediction across selected small-model families. Existing circuit analysis, NOP tests, compositional metrics, and attention-causal methods remain explicit baselines \\\\\\\\citep{ranmilo2026,fesser2026,papamichalis2026,franco2025}.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Pilot.} Pin revisions of GPT-2 124M and Pythia 160M, 410M, and 1B. Use 100 development and 200 disjoint test documents at lengths 128 and 512, with three sampling seeds. Seeds vary fixture selection; they do not turn one pretrained checkpoint into three independently trained models. Keep tokenization and model-supported position conventions fixed within every paired comparison.\\\\n\\\\nDefine each prediction example as a document by prespecified layer/KV-group intervention configuration. Within that configuration, patch K before query--key score computation and V before value aggregation: zero only the sink value while preserving its key, perturb only its key with a norm-matched nonsink key, and run a sham patch. Measure output after the head output-projection block. Check that the local attention weights are unchanged by the value-only intervention; later layers may change because their inputs have changed. Features include output-projected sink contribution, key-perturbation sensitivity, sink mass, and conditional content entropy. The target is excess next-token negative log likelihood (NLL) after a distinct intervention: mask all declared anchor positions at the same selected layer/KV group and renormalize attention, preserving surviving positions and frozen suffix states. Whole-model deletion is a separately labeled exploratory target. Fit development diagnostic features against development deletion labels. On each held-out document, acquire features using the frozen K/V diagnostic procedure without reading deletion labels; then score the frozen predictor against the separately obtained deletion outcome. All model/configuration observations from one source document stay together in splitting and resampling. This is document-level prediction, not replication of a development-only model signature across supposedly independent examples.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Controls and acceptance.} Fit a regularized predictor on development data only. Compare its test mean absolute error (MAE) with mass-only, norm-only, and feature-ablated baselines. Use document-cluster bootstrap for paired error differences. Freeze thresholds and head selection before test evaluation, include matched random-token and sham patches, and restore original K/V for rescue checks. Go forward only when the paired interval for MAE improvement excludes zero and controls are consistent with the claimed attribution. Leave-family-out transfer is exploratory because the family count is small. If it fails, release the error analysis rather than claim a universal sink classifier.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Priority 2: attribute anchor-switch boundary shocks}\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Question and hypothesis.} Does changing retained anchors create a short-lived predictive loss increase beyond suffix-recomputation effects? This is not another demonstration that keeping sinks stabilizes streaming. It isolates a counterfactual at a boundary, acknowledging that cache-local rotary positions and the origin of the first state matter \\\\\\\\citep{xiao2024,ruscio2026,kiya2026}.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Pilot.} Start with Pythia 160M, 410M, and 1B, a 512-position cache containing four anchors and a 508-token recent suffix, and prose/code streams up to 16K tokens. This is bounded-cache streaming, not a 16K dense-context claim. At declared boundaries, cross original anchors versus a controlled alternate-prefix anchor-state substitution with reused versus recomputed suffix states. Pin original anchor token IDs from positions 0--3 and construct alternate anchors by replaying an answer-free, development-selected four-token prefix at the same positions in the same model. Record both token-ID sets and provenance. Identical-prefix replay is a numerical no-op control, not a substantive reset treatment. The mixed-state arms are diagnostic interventions, not production reset policies; alternate token content/provenance changes are part of the treatment. For the recomputed-suffix arm, replay the exact recent suffix after the original four-token prefix, then freeze that resulting suffix in both anchor conditions. Compare anchor effects within each suffix arm and estimate their interaction. A matched nonsink-state substitution is needed before attributing effects specifically to sink function. Every arm uses the same model revision and isolated session; no cross-user state is shared.\\\\n\\\\nWithin each suffix-state arm, hold suffix tensors and cache-local positions identical. Generate keys before RoPE or correctly undo and reapply rotations when assigning positions. Test the unchanged-state path against a no-op implementation for numerical agreement. Absolute-position GPT-2 is not used for this streaming remapping experiment. Fresh recomputation must use the same intended retained input and no hidden information unavailable to the comparison arm.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Controls and acceptance.} The primary directional endpoint is signed mean excess NLL over the first 64 post-boundary tokens relative to that suffix arm's unchanged-anchor control. Positive-part excess-NLL area is a secondary severity endpoint, because it can be positive even when signed mean harm is zero. Also report peak excess loss and recovery: the first point after which loss remains within a development-fixed tolerance for a prespecified run of tokens. Prespecify the anchor-by-suffix interaction; compare with matched nonsink substitutions. Mark recovery as right-censored if the observation window ends before the recovery criterion is met. Sample 200 held-out stream boundaries, bootstrap by document rather than boundary, and report prose/code strata. Go forward only when an effect exceeds a development-fixed practical threshold, its interval excludes zero, and position/backend and matched nonsink-patch controls do not explain it. Otherwise reject anchor-specific attribution or identify an implementation defect. No old-fact recall gain is inferred from lower NLL \\\\\\\\citep{cao2026}.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Priority 3: test sink-value precision downgrades}\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Question and hypothesis.} Can selected sink KV groups use lower-precision values while preserving keys, without practically important excess loss near eviction? The contribution is a held-out, boundary-stratified noninferiority and sensitivity map, not asymmetric precision, a new sink detector, or small-model quantization itself \\\\\\\\citep{kivi2024,hariri2025,kvsink2025,subkv2025}.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Pilot.} Use Pythia 410M and 1B first, with cache capacities 256 and 512. Optionally add a current rotary grouped-query model after its configuration and kernels are audited. Evaluate K16/V16, K16/V4, K4/V16, and K4/V4 for protected groups while holding nonsink quantizers fixed. Use established per-channel key and per-token value axes, record pre-/post-RoPE choices, clipping, group size, scale storage, and zero points. In grouped-query attention (GQA), KV states are shared by query heads: policies must select KV groups, not pretend that each query head has independently stored keys and values.\\\\n\\\\nFreeze a group selection policy on development documents, then evaluate 200 independent held-out streams, domain shifts, and the 64-token post-eviction window. Compare first-N protection, KVSink, SubKV, random protection, recent-token protection, and symmetric sink preservation. Numerical sensitivity tests may first hold the set of cached tokens constant; deployment comparisons must additionally match total actual bytes by adjusting the cache budget or precision allocation. These are different experiments and should not be mixed in one superiority claim.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\textbf{Acceptance and early exit.} Report three numerical outcomes: noninferiority supported if the upper one-sided bound is below the margin; margin-exceeding harm supported if the lower one-sided bound is above it; and inconclusive otherwise. Failure to pass does not establish harm. A candidate downgrade passes numerical noninferiority only if the upper one-sided 95\\\\\\\\% document-bootstrap bound for excess NLL relative to symmetric protection is below a preregistered 0.01 nats/token margin. That margin is a proposed engineering tolerance, not a literature-established standard. Prespecified domain/boundary strata must also satisfy it; use a simultaneous bootstrap upper bound across strata, or a conservative multiplicity adjustment. An engineering go additionally requires at least 1\\\\\\\\% measured total-cache savings and no latency regression in a real backend. Fake quantization demonstrates sensitivity, not storage reduction or throughput.\\\\n\\\\nBefore implementation, bound possible savings. For a 512-token cache, four protected tokens, otherwise K4/V4, and protected K16/V16, payload bits per shared layer/head dimension are $508(4+4)+4(16+16)=4192$. Lowering only four protected values from 16 to 4 bits saves $4(16-4)=48$ bits per dimension, or about 1.15\\\\\\\\% of this payload. At 4096 tokens the same change is roughly 0.15\\\\\\\\%. Metadata, residual buffers, and incomplete protected groups can reduce either percentage further. Thus a prefix-only policy may fail the engineering threshold even if numerically sound. Report sink mass and conditional content entropy separately, following the already-published distinction \\\\\\\\citep{papamichalis2026}. When $1-s_i$ is effectively zero, flag the content estimate as unavailable rather than divide by zero or invent precision. Report its magnitude relative to the full head output and residual state, with explicit treatment of near-zero denominators. This is an intervention feature, not a proof that an apparently small component is causally irrelevant: cancellation, downstream amplification, and multihead compensation can all matter. Removing a token's direct KV entry removes direct access to that entry, but later cached states were computed from its past context and may contain indirect traces. Exact ``cannot influence the output'' statements therefore require identical retained state or an appropriate recomputation/counterfactual construction. The first causal token has no access to future content, whereas later anchors can encode their own preceding prefix. This distinction is essential for both the boundary audit and the optional oracle-retrieval branch. Fluent indefinite streaming is never equated with indefinite factual recall \\\\\\\\citep{xiao2024,cao2026}.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\\\\subsection{Resource envelope and staging}\\\\nThe preferred work is inference-only. As a planning estimate, 1B parameters at two bytes per weight require approximately 2 GB for weights alone, before loading overhead, activations, caches, and framework state. A 16--24 GB accelerator is a plausible pilot target when models run sequentially and hooks stream summaries, but no device benchmark was executed here. Materializing all attention maps scales as $LHT^2$ and can dominate memory. Restrict hooks to selected layers, use batch size one during validation, and aggregate statistics rather than retaining every matrix.\\\\n\\\\nThe 200-stream counts are pilot planning targets, not power guarantees. Use development-only variance estimates to plan interval precision before final freezing. Use equal-document weighting of paired mean NLL or prediction error; cluster all configurations, repeated seeds, and boundaries from one document. Select nonoverlapping boundary windows: mark an eviction event, score 64 tokens, and do not score another event from the same stream inside that interval. Stage B runs the harm predictor and boundary audit on 410M/1B models after fixture checks. Stage C attempts precision deployment only after the savings bound and simulated noninferiority screen pass. Expansion to new architectures requires separate tokenizer and configuration audits. Public corpus licensing, checkpoint revisions, quantizer versions, random seeds, and dataset splits belong in the run manifest.
